title: Fibonacci common-bar scope as a contextual quantity-writing mechanism
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. The same written fraction cells have globally constrained, different values under a common bar, separate bars and reversed scope. Complete source notation binds repeated components through nested denominators; target numeral spelling and serialization remain unknown.

source_evidence.quote: ## A. Fibonacci: common-bar scope changes the values of earlier components

source.author: Fibonacci
source.ownership: Complete bounded notation primer, including special circle and subsidiary-bar constructions, inventoried in source dossier.

design.new_consequence: Appending cells inside one common bar changes every earlier component through additional denominators; a separate bar terminates that scope. The same cells therefore have different values without changing their local numeral identity.

finite_semantic_productions.concatenation: V(A B)=V(B)+V(A)/D(B), with D the product of denominator cells
finite_semantic_productions.separate_bars: sum of independently evaluated bar values
finite_semantic_productions.scope: Ordinary common-bar and separate-bar constructions only. Other marked constructions remain explicitly inventoried; they are not fallback parses.

complete_owned_examples.zero_policy: Zero retains the7-denominator grade; deleting the cell is not equivalent.
